comparison: Both evaluate the GAL-induced ncRNA system and hybrid formation at the YAC locus (C40-C48). OpenEval finds the DIP data and functional instability assays sufficient. Peer reviewers request more precise transcription analysis (RNAseq or Northern) and direct S9.6 DIP/ChIP detection of R-loops at ncRNA positions, indicating current evidence is insufficient.

Both address RNase H mutant hybrids being RAD51-independent (C59-C62). OpenEval finds the cytological and functional data sufficient to demonstrate alternative hybrid formation mechanisms. Peer reviewers apply general concerns about S9.6 quantification and specificity controls to these experiments, requiring statistical analysis before full acceptance.

Both evaluate trans hybrid formation (C6, C64-C75). OpenEval finds the DIP molecular evidence and functional instability data with structural characterization sufficient. Peer reviewers specifically emphasize that direct S9.6 DIP/ChIP detection is especially important for trans experiments and request controls for homology requirements, indicating the evidence needs strengthening.

Both address Srs2p as anti-hybrid factor (C8, C10, C82-C87). OpenEval finds the Rad51p-dependent hybrid increase in srs2Δ with specificity controls sufficient. Peer reviewers request testing other anti-hybrid factors (SEN1, TOP1/2) for comparison and statistical analysis of S9.6 staining, indicating quantification needs improvement.

Both address whether Rad51p binding precedes DNA damage (C56-C57). OpenEval finds the γ-H2AX absence and timing data sufficient, though acknowledges alternative explanations. Peer reviewers identify this as central to the major issue of direct versus indirect Rad51p effects and suggest HO cleavage experiments, indicating current evidence insufficient to definitively establish mechanism.

Both address Rad51p ChIP at hybrid-forming locus and mechanistic claims (C4, C5, C49-C55). OpenEval finds ChIP data with spatial/temporal controls sufficient, noting C4 involves mechanistic inference. Peer reviewers identify this as 'the major issue,' stating it's impossible to exclude combined effects on recombination and hybrid promotion, requesting acknowledgment of this limitation.

Both address Rad52p effects on hybrids (C76-C78). OpenEval finds the parallel suppression by RAD52 deletion sufficient given known Rad52p-Rad51p relationship. Peer reviewers' concerns about S9.6 quantification and specificity controls (points 1-2) apply to these experiments, requiring statistical analysis and additional validation.

Both evaluate RAD51 deletion suppressing hybrids in RNA biogenesis mutants (C2, C31-C38). OpenEval finds converging cytological and functional evidence sufficient. Peer reviewers request statistical analysis of S9.6 immunofluorescence and additional specificity controls (RNase H sensitivity, transcription dependence, nuclear localization), indicating more rigorous quantification needed.

OpenEval evaluates S9.6 antibody specificity validation (C95-C97) from prior work showing RNase H sensitivity. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this, though peer point 2 requests additional S9.6 specificity controls, suggesting they want more validation beyond what's cited.

OpenEval evaluates speculative claims about trans hybrid amplification and cancer relevance (C7, C90), finding them uncertain due to limited direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these speculative claims are not central to the experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates synthesis claims about non-redundant anti-hybrid pathways (C93-C94), finding them well-supported by accumulated evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers focus on experimental validation rather than synthetic conclusions.
